sentences.text: Shri Anoop Saxena, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Neeraj Ashar, learned P.L. for the respondent/State.
Heard on the question of admission.
Revision is admitted for hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.21875/2018, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.

The revision has been preferred by the applicant against judgment dated 20.11.2018 passed by learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge Chhatarpur, District Chhatarpur in Criminal Appeal No.70/2015 whereby the learned Appellate Court has partly allowed the appeal and modified the judgment of conviction of the Criminal Case No.1508/2008, passed by Presiding Judicial Magistrate First Class Chhatarpur, District Chhatarpur (M.P.). vide order dated 30.01.2015.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Applicant stands convicted for an offence punishable under Section 7 (I) read with Section 16(1) d (II) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, and has been sentenced to undergo RI for 6 months with fine of Rs.2000/- in default of payment of fine additional R.I. for 3 months.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail.
He also submits that there are many contradictions, omissions and improvements in the version of the prosecution witnesses.

The Food Inspector was having no power and authority to initiate the proceedings against the present applicant because the place where the alleged incident of proceedings have been initiated, comes under the territorial jurisdiction of Nagar Palik Parisad Chhatarpur, under which only local self authorities are empowered to initiate the proceedings, as the Food Inspector is available in the Nagar Palika.
No independent witnesses have supported the case of the 2 CRR-6165-2018 prosecution.

At the time of pronouncement of Appellate Judgement, the appellant was not present before the Appellant Court, therefore, a supersession warrant has been issued against the appellant and on 13.12.2018 the appellant has surrendered himself before the concerning Court and since then he is in jail.
He further submits that there is fair chance to succeed in the case.
The final hearing of this revision will take time.
If the applicant is not released on bail, purpose of filing this application will be frustrated.
Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the applicant may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned P.L. has opposed the application.

After having heard rival submissions at length, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case,
but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicant and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No.21875/2018 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.
The custodial sentence awarded to the applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision.

Applicant Babbu @ Pappu be released from custody subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

The applicant shall appear and mark his presence before the trial Court on 24.02.2019 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates as may be given in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
List the revision for final hearing in due course of time at its own turn.
C.C. as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR SRIVASTAVA) JUDGE sp Babbu @ Pappu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130532339/
